ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$, and $\angle DAC=\angle B$. Point $E$ is on $AD$, with $CD=CE$. $\triangle ACE\sim \triangle BAD$: If $AB=10$, and $BC=6$, determine the length of the line segment $AD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
thus $CD = BD = CE = \frac{1}{2} BC = 3$,\\
since $\angle DAC = \angle B$, it follows that $\angle ACD = \angle BCA$, and thus $\triangle ACD \sim \triangle BCA$,\\
so $\frac{AC}{BC} = \frac{CD}{AC}$, that is, $\frac{AC}{6} = \frac{3}{AC}$,\\
which leads to $AC = 3\sqrt{2}$. Given that $\triangle ACE \sim \triangle BAD$,\\
we have $\frac{AC}{BA} = \frac{CE}{AD}$, that is, $\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{10} = \frac{3}{AD}$,\\
therefore $AD = \boxed{5\sqrt{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC; B, D, C are on the same horizontal base BC, with D located between B and C; A is above, and line segment AD connects from A to D; point E is on AD; line segments AC, AB, and CE are also drawn. It can be seen from the figure that D is on BC, so CD and CB are collinear. Reasoning: Because AD is the median of triangle ABC, and BC=6, D is the midpoint of BC, and BD=CD=3. It is also known that CD=CE, therefore CE=3. Since D is on BC, ray CD and CB are collinear, so ∠ACD=∠BCA. The problem statement gives ∠DAC=∠B, therefore triangle ACD and triangle BCA have two pairs of corresponding angles equal, hence △ACD∼△BCA. According to the correspondence, AC corresponds to BC, and CD corresponds to AC, so AC/BC=CD/AC. Substituting BC=6 and CD=3 gives AC/6=3/AC, therefore AC^2=18, AC=3√2. Also, the problem statement says △ACE∼△BAD; according to the similarity order, AC corresponds to BA, and CE corresponds to AD, so AC/BA=CE/AD. Substituting AC=3√2, BA=10, and CE=3 gives (3√2)/10=3/AD, solving gives AD=5√2.
